item.title: Duane Falley
item.description: Duane Daniel Falley, 63, of Victoria, KS died Saturday, February 14, 2026 at Melvern, Kansas at his farm where he and his wife Lynda planned to retire. He was born February 22, 1963 in Quinter, KS the son of Warren and Patricia (Younger) Falley. He received a Lucky High School diploma and graduated from Manhattan Area Technical College with a welding degree. He would then move to Victoria, KS in 1998. item.title: Clarence D McIlvain
item.description: Clarence D. McIlvain, age 84, of Ottawa, Kansas, passed away on March 3, 2026, at The University of Kansas Health System-Olathe in Olathe, Kansas. Born on October 9, 1941, in Madison, Kansas, Clarence was the beloved son of Robert Earl and Mary Elizabeth (Lewis) McIlvain. He grew up in a family that moved frequently, spending his formative years in various towns across Kansas, including Madison, Kechi, Lane, graduating with the class of 1960, and Centropolis. item.title: GARY KUNTZ
item.description: If you haven’t heard, a former Ottawa High School teacher that had an impact on Ottawa beyond the classroom walls, has passed away. Gary Kuntz, who taught math in the Ottawa school district for 37 years died February 28th. Kuntz was passionately dedicated to Babe Ruth Baseball in Ottawa and spent over 20 years as the State Commissioner. item.title: NO CANDY OF POP WITH KS SNAP DOLLARS
item.description: Kansas is joining other states in putting restrictions on candy and soda with its Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, known as SNAP. Governor Laura Kelly announced yesterday, March 4th, that Kansas is joining 21 other states in implementing the restriction on candy and soda with SNAP dollars. She says she has always supported policies that incentivize healthy eating. item.title: Carl D Hornbuckle
item.description: Carl DeWayne Hornbuckle, 81, of Ottawa, Kansas, passed away at his home on March 2, 2026. He was born May 26, 1944, in Ottawa, Kansas, to James Maxwell Hornbuckle and Ruby Oneita (Hoover) Hornbuckle. A lifelong resident of Ottawa, Carl attended Lincoln Elementary School and Ottawa Junior High School before graduating from Ottawa High School with the Class of 1962.
